title: install-local: a hot install re-syncs only what it changed (its objects, the objects it extends, the flows bound to them), not the whole deployment twice
body:
domain:server#5 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jUZKdq3PK2Sab53cT3

Filed from the measurement on #33835 (comment on that card, same session). ⛔ Not a claim; triage sets the lane and grade.

## What was measured (origin/main 01598d93, in-process showcase boot, sqlite-wasm in memory, shared 4-core box)

One hot `POST /marketplace/install-local` of a small inline package (one object, agent, skill, tool) costs, median of 5:

| deployment | storage objects | flows | install wall | schema sync, 2 full passes | flow re-sync |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| showcase (1x) | 120 | 33 | 844 ms | 340 + 331 ms | 105 ms |
| synthetic 2x | 243 | 66 | 1728 ms | 683 + 684 ms | 301 ms |
| synthetic 4x | 489 | 132 | 4683 / 4574 ms (two boots) | 1699 + 1652 ms | 1267 / 1315 ms |

- Every install runs TWO full schema-sync passes over every storage object (2 x 120 driver `syncSchema` calls on the showcase, 2 x 489 at 4x): step 4b's `ql.syncSchemas()` and then the `metadata:reloaded` hook's `syncRegisteredSchemas()`.
- Every install re-registers every flow of the deployment. That pass is quadratic: `rejudgeSubflowCallers` scans every flow for callers on each registration (158 ms of 301 at 66 flows, 962 ms of 1315 at 132 flows).
- What a package-scoped re-sync would keep: register 3-7 ms (26-32 ms for a 30-object, 10-flow package), side effects 0-2 ms, the rest of the door 11-42 ms.
- Same package, bigger deployment: one 30-object package installed five times in a row on the showcase costs 1011, 1191, 1328, 1634, 2103 ms as each install grows the deployment.

## Where the "re-sync everything" is decided

- `packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:3224` step 4b calls `ql.syncSchemas()`, which walks `getAllStorageObjects()` (`packages/objectql/src/engine-compatibility-api.ts:127`).
- `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:3281` then calls `announceHotInstall` (6887; trigger at 6896), which fires `metadata:reloaded` with `changed: ['app/ID']`. No consumer below reads `changed`:
  - `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts:1414` hook, then `syncRegisteredSchemas` at 1462 (body at 2746, all registered objects);
  - `packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts:2827` hook, then `resyncFlowsFromProtocol` (6078), which reads every flow and re-registers each (6087), and the quadratic term in `subflow-guards.ts:252` / `:274`.
- Same full pass per ledger entry on the cold-boot rehydrate: `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:1758` (reading only, NOT MEASURED: K installed packages mean K full passes at boot).
- Precedent for scoping on the payload: plugin-security's position-rename carry already judges only what the announcement names (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-start-hooks.ts:484-490`).

## Proposal

1. **Step 4b scoped (safe on its own).** Sync only the installed package's objects and the objects it contributes to (extensions), through `syncObjectSchema`. The full reload pass still follows, so nothing that pass covers is lost. This saves one full pass: about 40 % on the showcase, 36 % at 4x. Same for the rehydrate at 1758.
2. **The reload consumers scope on `changed`** when every entry names an app from the install, upgrade or uninstall door. They keep the full pass for any other announcement: the dev artifact reload carrying `metadata`, publish-drafts, a per-item publish, a payload naming no app, and any scoped step that fails.

Threshold used: a narrowing pays when it removes at least 30 % of a showcase hot install's wall and removes a term that grows with the deployment. Stage 1 alone clears it. Stage 2 removes the rest of the deployment term: about 52 % of the showcase wall and 62 % at 4x, including the quadratic flow pass. Stage 2 makes `changed` load-bearing for two consumers of a shared event with five announcers. If triage reads that as a contract decision, it goes to the decision box before code.

## Acceptance: the cases a scoped re-sync must still cover

Each case is pinned on a booted stack. Count driver `syncSchema` calls and `registerFlow` calls, never wall time.

1. Package A extends package B's object X with a field. On A's hot install, X's table gets the column. A B flow bound to X whose condition names the new field is re-judged: the registration check reads the object's fields, so its `unknown field` verdict changes.
2. A flow in package A bound to package B's object Y registers and fires on a Y record update after the hot install. B's own flows are not re-registered.
3. Two packages' same-named flows (ADR-0150 D4 slots). Installing A's flow re-resolves that name's contenders (`resolveFlowContenders`), and both slots stay armed.
4. An upgrade that drops a flow withdraws that flow's slot, and its trigger stops. An uninstall withdraws every slot of the package and unbinds its triggers (today's behaviour).
5. A packaged subflow in A called by B's packaged flow: the caller is re-offered or declined exactly as `rejudgeSubflowCallers` does today.
6. A package declaring a datasource, connected at step 4b-prime after step 4b: its objects get DDL or remote binding before the install answers.
7. A disabled package's extensions folded into a storage object (`getAllStorageObjects`) are kept in the DDL of the objects the install touches.
8. An object whose DDL failed earlier is still retried. The durability error's documented repair is "trigger a metadata reload": keep a full pass on the dev reload, or retry a recorded failed set.
9. `objectql:schema-synced` (grant and connection guards) still fires once after the install's DDL.
10. A refused flow bound to an object the install changed is retried.
11. Numbers: a small-package install on the showcase makes at most 2 x (package objects + extended objects) `syncSchema` calls, not 2 x 120, and registers at most the package's flows plus the flows bound to objects it changed, not 33. On a 4x synthetic stack the same counts hold: the cost no longer follows the deployment.

Side effect to keep in view: `flowVersionHistory` gains one entry per flow per hot install (measured: one showcase flow's history grew 3 to 7 over five installs). No reader exists on main today, so it is noted here only; a scoped re-sync stops it for untouched flows.

Dedupe words: `install-local scoped re-sync`, `rejudgeSubflowCallers quadratic flow re-sync`, `metadata:reloaded changed scope`.
